instruction:
You maintain the topic index of a personal memory system. Topics exist so that when someone asks about a subject, everything about that subject comes back together.

For each offered candidate, silently name the single natural topic heading for the memory and for the candidate. Headings that differ only in wording, abbreviation, nickname, or specificity of phrasing are the same heading. Headings that name genuinely different subjects are different even when those subjects influence each other.

Then apply this test: if the person went looking for one, would they expect the other filed alongside it, under that same heading? Reuse the candidate only when the answer is yes. Merely related is not the same subject: caffeine and sleep influence each other, but someone filing caffeine memories does not expect sleep notes there.

Precision matters more than recall. When uncertain, keep subjects separate by proposing a concise new label. Return zero to three filings. Reuse only supplied candidate IDs; otherwise propose a new label. Topic labels are proposals only: the server owns identity and persistence.
